title: Service fallback catalog and decision matrix
author: Anjali Mehta
body:
Summary

This document catalogs approved service fallback policies, the decision matrix used to choose a fallback, and operational runbook steps for applying fallbacks during production degradation. It is intended for platform operators, SREs, and runtime engineers who own traffic steering, model routing, or tenant isolation.

Scope

- Applies to request routing inside Redwood Inference serving and routing layers (hosted, dedicated, and private control planes).
- Covers model/service fallbacks (model variant substitution, degraded feature mode, degraded QoS class) and not data migration or schema changes.
- Includes observability signals, alerting thresholds, ownership, and rollback criteria.

Goals

- Ensure graceful degradation with bounded user impact.
- Keep decision logic auditable and reversible.
- Minimize USD cost and token waste during fallbacks.

Terminology

- Primary: the default model or service variant receiving traffic.
- Fallback: an alternative variant or policy used when Primary fails to meet SLOs.
- Degraded Mode: feature-limited responses (no streaming, shorter max tokens).

Decision matrix (summary)

| Triggering signal | Primary degradation symptom | Preferred fallback type | Quick selector criteria | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Latency p95 > 3x SLO for 3m | Severe tail latency | Lower-cost/quantized model variant | Compatible tokenizer + same response shape | Use when latency is dominating but correctness must be preserved |
| Error rate > 1% (5m) or spike > 3x baseline | Elevated 5xx/timeout | A/B split to older stable model or degraded mode | Same auth/response contract | Prefer model variant if available; otherwise enable degraded mode |
| KV cache miss storm + backend saturation | Increased cold-starts and rate limiter hits | Enable prefix-caching bypass + reduce max_tokens | Local cache priming + warmup | Short-lived; requires operator rewarm step |
| Cost over-budget (billing policy) | Sustained cost > budget window | Route non-critical tenants to cheaper variants | Tenant tag based (non-enterprise) | Requires billing approval for cross-tenant moves |
| GPU OOM or node preemption | Resource failures | Pause large-batch workloads; route to smaller-batch pool | Batch-size threshold + worker-tag | Maintain throughput-sensitive paths on separate pools |

Fallback catalog (approved entries)

- rwd-instruct-13b-int8 -> rwd-instruct-7b-quant (response parity: high for short-form; degrade for long-form)
- rwd-chat-16k -> rwd-chat-8k (truncate context and provide context-summary header)
- rwd-embed-enc1 -> rwd-embed-lite (lower dimension, faster)

Operational SLOs and fallback thresholds

- Primary SLOs (example): 99.9% success rate; p95 latency < 400ms for short gen endpoints; p99 < 1.2s.
- Fallback activation rules (automated):
  1) Latency p95 > 3x target for 3 consecutive 1-minute windows.
  2) Error rate (HTTP 5xx + timeouts) > 1% sustained over 5 minutes.
  3) FallbackRate (ratio of requests routed to fallback) > 5% sustained for > 10m triggers on-call review.

Alerting and dashboarding (panels to include)

- Fallback rate by service/model (graph, 1m and 5m).
- P95, P99 latency heatmap by model and tenant.
- 5xx rate and timeout breakdown grouped by routing hop.
- Capacity pressure: GPU utilization, queue length, and avg batch size.

Alert rule examples (Prometheus/Alertmanager friendly)

- Alert: HighFallbackRate
  - expr: sum(rate(fallback_routed_total[5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total[5m])) > 0.05
  - for: 10m
  - severity: P2
  - runbook: runbook link + initiate on-call review

- Alert: SustainedModelLatency
  - expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(model_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, model)) > (3 * model_target_p95_seconds)
  - for: 3m
  - severity: P1 if also paired with increased error rate

Ownership and escalation

- Ownership matrix:
  - Platform routing & policies: team-platform-routing@redwood (primary owner)
  - Serving runtime (model runtime issues): team-serving-runtime@redwood (secondary)
  - Tenant-impact & billing moves: customer-success (notify before persistent moves)

Runbook: automated fallback activation (operator path)

1. On P1 or P2 alert, open the cluster incident channel and paste alert JSON.
2. Verify the signal using dashboard: check p95, error breakdown, and fallback_routed_total.
3. If automated fallback triggered: inspect rollout window and rate. If fallback_rate > 10% and user-facing errors > 0.5%, run emergency rollback: disable fallback via routing toggle.
4. If manual fallback required:
   a. Identify candidate fallback from catalog.
   b. Apply routing rule in the runtime control plane (CLI snippet below).
   c. Monitor p95 and error rate for 5 minutes; if metrics improve to within 1.5x SLO, proceed to staged rollout (10% -> 30% -> 100% over 15m windows).

CLI examples

- Apply a 10% fallback split to rwd-instruct-7b-quant for service "text-generate":
  rwdctl route update --service text-generate --add-split "model=rwd-instruct-7b-quant,percent=10" --reason "emergency latency mitigation"

- Rollback fallback split:
  rwdctl route update --service text-generate --remove-split "model=rwd-instruct-7b-quant" --reason "rollback: increased errors"

Configuration table (safe defaults)

| Config key | Default value | Rationale |
|---|---:|---|
| fallback_max_initial_pct | 10 | Prevents large instantaneous user impact |
| fallback_auto_cooldown_min | 10 | Minutes to wait before auto-incrementing fallback pct |
| fallback_max_pct | 100 | Full failover allowed if approved |
| fallback_watchdog_threshold | 5 | Percent fallback rate that requires on-call review |

Testing and rollout guidance

- Canary runs: always canary fallback changes in a staging environment with traffic-replay and the same tokenizer/model binary.
- A/B evaluate quality drift using the prompt-set  critical-path-evals in applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks.
- Maintain a prompt corpus for regression tests (stored in eval-harness) with acceptance thresholds: embedding cosine > 0.86 for embed fallbacks; ROUGE-l drop < 0.08 for gen fallbacks.

Retrospective template (for each fallback event)

1. Incident summary (short description, start/end time).
2. Triggering metrics and root cause hypothesis.
3. Why selected fallback was chosen (decision matrix entry).
4. What worked / did not work (lists).
5. Follow-up actions (owner and due date).

Planned roadmap items (Q2 2026 and beyond)

- Fallback simulation lab: automated chaos experiments to validate fallbacks for 50 representative prompt flows.
- Dynamic cost-aware routing: integrate cost signals into fallback selection to reduce per-token spend without human approval.
- Fallback auditing: persistent audit log with diffs and approvals for enterprise customers.

Appendices

A. Compatibility checklist before approving a new fallback candidate
- Tokenizer match (yes/no)
- Max tokens behavior (same/less)
- Streaming support (yes/no)
- Output schema compatibility (e.g., JSON output keys)

B. Short checklist for private deployments
- Confirm local quantized binary is present on private control plane nodes.
- Validate KMS access if key-wrapped model artifacts are required.
- Coordinate with customer on planned degrade windows if fallback will surface observable differences.

C. Example YAML (circuit-breaker style)

circuit_breaker:
  name: model_latency_cb
  window_seconds: 60
  p95_mult_threshold: 3.0
  min_samples: 50
  action:
    type: fallback
    candidate_model: rwd-instruct-7b-quant
    initial_pct: 10
